title: One Act, Many Masks: Effect-Marginal Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.29427v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent advances in multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) have substantially improved the performance of LLM agents on complex, long-horizon interactive tasks. However, despite progress in fine-grained credit assignment, policy optimization still applies these learning signals through response-specific probability ratios. Different textual responses can induce the same executable effect, yet credit differences arising from subsequent outcomes remain tied to their individual textual realizations. We identify this mismatch as credit-update misalignment. Our analysis reveals that credit-text pairing directly shapes policy-update directions, even when the policy context and executable effect are held fixed. translated_title: 一幕多面：面向长程智能体的效应边缘策略优化
translated_abstract: 多轮强化学习（RL）的最新进展显著提升了LLM智能体在复杂、长程交互任务上的性能。然而，尽管在细粒度信用分配方面已取得进展，策略优化仍通过针对特定响应的概率比来应用这些学习信号。不同的文本响应可以产生相同的可执行效应，但由后续结果产生的信用差异仍然与各自的文本实现绑定在一起。我们将这种不匹配识别为“信用更新错位”。我们的分析揭示，即使策略上下文和可执行效应保持不变，信用与文本的配对方式也会直接塑造策略更新的方向。受这一发现启发，我们提出了效应边缘策略优化（EMPO），它通过一个效应级别的代理目标将不同文本实现之间的更新耦合起来，使策略优化与执行层面的等价性保持一致……
tldr: 该论文发现了多轮强化学习中信用信号与具体文本响应绑定所导致的“信用更新错位”问题，并提出效应边缘策略优化（EMPO），通过效应级别的代理目标将策略更新与执行层面的等价性对齐，从而改进长程LLM智能体的策略优化。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies "credit-update misalignment" in multi-turn RL, where credit signals remain tied to specific textual responses even when they induce identical executable effects, and proposes Effect-Marginal Policy Optimization (EMPO), which aligns policy updates with execution-level equivalence through an effect-level surrogate objective for long-horizon LLM agents.
